measuredOn: AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 16 threads, Fedora 44, Node v24.14.1, npm run build. Unlike tests/long-journal/budgets.json's timing budgets this carries no machine-speed multiplier - the same source and the same lockfile gzip to close to the same byte count on any machine - but it is not bit-for-bit reproducible either: five straight rebuilds of one commit, no source change between them, gzipped to 295868-295884B. Vite/Rollup's content hashing is not fully deterministic run to run. gzipBytesBudget carries a 1024B floor over the baseline for exactly that (GZIP_WOBBLE_FLOOR_BYTES in check-first-load-budget.mjs), the same job FLOOR_MS does for the timing budgets. filesBudget carries none - the file count was the same 111 across all five rebuilds. Seeded at 295873B across 111 files for phase 9 audit ticket 01, which is the ratchet tickets 02 and 03 tighten rather than a target anybody has agreed. Re-record with `node scripts/check-first-load-budget.mjs --record` after a change that is meant to grow the first-load graph, and paste the printed block in here. Ticket 03 tightened it on 2026-09-06, on this same machine: 258412B across 109 files, from deferring the archive and hormone-curve areas out of journal.ts's composition and moving fractionalEpochDay off the path that kept the curve models in the graph anyway. Its baseline is not the 295873B above but a fresh measurement of main taken the same afternoon, 295878B across the same 111 files, because tickets 02, 04 and the migration squash had all landed in between and none of them re-recorded here. So the cut is 37466B, 12.7%, and two fewer round trips. Phase 9 audit ticket 13 then bisected the window between ticket 01's baseline and ticket 03's rebaseline for a specific claim: that ticket 02 removing d3-shape/d3-scale's ~22.5KB chunk left a gap something else refilled almost exactly, one for one. Building main at 5e2454df (before ticket 02), d1388cce (ticket 02's own merge) and af799505 (the migration squash) measured 297018B/113 files, then 297039B/113 files, then 297041B/113 files - a 23B spread across three commits, inside this file's own 1024B wobble floor, the same 113 files at every point, and every asset with a readable name (0.css, AccessModeSetup.css, DatePicker.css, flatpickrLocale.css) byte-identical across all three builds. There is no chunk to attribute, because d3 was not in the shipped bundle to begin with at 5e2454df - ticket 02's fix closed a hole in the source-import graph, not in the bytes a browser downloads, so nothing needed replacing. The 295873B/111-to-295878B/111 arithmetic that looked like a one-for-one swap was two measurements taken against this file's already-stale baseline at different times, not a delta anyone had actually built and measured. The rule that follows from it, matching the obligation budgets.json's four mount ratchets already carry: re-record only against a change you can name, and name it here, in this note, the way every entry above does. A fresh build of main disagreeing with the recorded baseline for a reason nobody can name is a finding, not a rebaseline - write it up and leave the number alone, unless you are the one closing that specific gap, in which case re-record only once you have brought the number back to or under where it started, never up to wherever main had drifted. Re-recorded here on 2026-09-06 for an unrelated, later reason: main had drifted to 113 files/261559B against the 109/258412B ticket 03 left behind, entirely from tickets 04 through 11 landing afterward without re-recording. Ticket au-11's progress bar is the one visibly-named addition (assets/progress.*.css); the rest is ordinary anonymous-chunk churn from six tickets' worth of real feature and fix work, too small individually to isolate and not a regression to chase. 4 files/3147B is the honest cost of shipping that work, recorded so the ratchet means something again.
